title: Victim's family drops A'burg police lawsuit
article: A $1-million lawsuit brought against Amherstburg police by the family of a man shot dead by an officer in 2000 will not proceed.

Town of Amherstburg lawyer Armando DeLuca confirmed the lawsuit by the family of Robert Scott Carpenter "has been withdrawn" but referred further questions to the London legal firm Harrison and Penza who represent the police service's insurance company.
"They handled it, it's done and the file is dead," said DeLuca.
Harrison and Penza could not be reached for comment Tuesday evening.
Carpenter, 36, died on Oct. 30, 2000, when Const. Shawn McCurdy shot him in the groin after a disrupted 911 call from Carpenter's common-law wife Lisa Stewart.
The suit sought damages for funeral costs, legal costs, loss of potential income costs and punitive damages in the amount of $1,081,843.29.
The plaintiffs in the suit included Carpenter's parents, Scott and Janet, and Carpenter's two children, Sarah and Noah.
The lawsuit, handled by Windsor lawyer Patrick Ducharme, alleged McCurdy "acted carelessly, recklessly and with wanton disregard" when he shot and killed Carpenter.
Ducharme could not be reached for comment Tuesday night.
DeLuca said notice came to the town a "couple of weeks ago" that the victim's family decided not to proceed with the lawsuit.
An investigation by the province's Special Investigations Unit cleared all the officers involved of any wrongdoing.
A coroner's inquest heard divergent testimony from several witnesses about what happened leading up to the shooting.
The 17 recommendations to come out of the inquest dealt more with the failings of Bell Canada's 911 system rather than police procedure or use of force.
